Paper_name: Prioritization of arbitrary faces associated to self: An EEG study
Summary: This study investigated the time course of preferential processing for self-related information using EEG. In two experiments, participants associated unfamiliar faces with verbal labels for self, friend, or stranger, then performed a matching task. Results showed faster reaction times and a more pronounced late frontal positivity when the first stimulus was self-associated. A central-parietal P3 following the second stimulus was enhanced when preceded by a self-related first stimulus, indicating facilitated processing of ensuing stimuli after self-representation activation.
Author: Mateusz Woźniak, Dimitrios Kourtis, Günther Knoblich
Conclusion: The study concludes that even unfamiliar faces associated with the self can activate a self-representation. Once activated, this self-representation facilitates the processing of subsequent stimuli, regardless of whether those stimuli are themselves self-associated. This is evidenced by faster reaction times and specific ERP components (late frontal positivity and central-parietal P3) linked to self-related first stimuli.
